answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to maintain a unique, time-locked computational stake that grows with participation. Agents must periodically solve personalized puzzles whose difficulty scales with claimed influence; cheap fakes fail. Picture umber-hued agents that wander a digital lagoon of verified interactions—only those with consistent, non-duplicable histories earn trust, as forging parallel identities multiplies the resource cost beyond profitability.
